headline: A group of mathematicians chaired by Terence Tao has urged colleagues to stop working with OpenAI after it released more than 700 AI-written maths papers in one go.
score_reason: Solid and widely relevant to the field, but the statement dates from 7 Oct, so one point below the pool score.
importance_line: Mathematicians now face hundreds of dense AI-written papers they must check by hand, and the field is split between boycott and engagement; the boycott is one group's position, not a field-wide decision.
summary: The Decoder reports that the Association for Human Mathematics, chaired by Fields Medalist Terence Tao, accuses OpenAI of breaking core research norms and urges mathematicians to stop working with the company, calling the release of more than 700 files at once "not a demonstration of scholarship, but a demonstration of power". The statement answers OpenAI's release of 722 maths manuscripts from an unreleased AI model, which we carried on 7 Oct 2026 from The Verge; The Decoder adds that many of the papers are so dense that even leading experts need AI help to read them.
notes: Read in full. Reply to the OpenAI release (X30 of 7 Oct 2026). Overlaps C04-06, C04-07, C04-17.
